en: The Jātaka:
The Fifth Collection, Chapter on the Arising of Beauty.
10. The Palāsa Jātaka “The swan said to the palāsa tree:
‘O friend, you shall grow into a nigrodha tree.’”
“Even as he sits upon your lap,
he will cut through your vital organs.
“The banyan tree shall only grow larger,” [he replied].
"I shall become his support;
he will be to me just as my father and mother are."
“That terrifying milk-tree which you have nurtured in your lap—
come, let us address it and depart.”
“Growth does not please him.
“Now indeed he fears me,
at the sight of the great ocean.”
"Because I did not understand the swan, a great fear has come upon me.
"His growth is not praised by the wise; [it is not that of one who has attained the goal]."
"He who, growing strong, devours his own foundation—
fearing such an obstruction,
the wise man laid a snare for his destruction."
The Palāsa Jātaka, the tenth.
The Second Chapter: On the Ascent of Color.
